verdict_reasoning: The goal has lasting demand, so level 1b does not fail, but level 2 does. prior-attempts-1 shows the series keeps the hand-written deparser design that [P1] was withdrawn over, and its replay test only counts declined commands. replication-ondisk-1 and replication-ondisk-2 show the intent-preserving rule lets publisher and subscriber diverge on implicit names and session settings. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 14 messages are visible.

brief.title: DDL deparser for CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE with JSON output
brief.problem: An event trigger sees that a DDL command ran but cannot reproduce it elsewhere, because the query string depends on search_path and parse analysis rewrites clauses. The main target is logical replication of DDL; auditing and schema synchronization are also named. The author also asks whether a deparser should preserve user intent or rebuild catalog state, as pg_get_table_ddl() does.
brief.proposed_design: The deparser takes the raw parse tree plus the catalogs and builds a self-documenting JSON blob, which ddl_json.c expands back into SQL. It preserves user intent: it omits clauses the user did not write, keeps serial as serial, schema-qualifies names, and does not split one command into several. The ALTER COLUMN TYPE ... USING text is captured during execution, before a sibling DROP COLUMN removes a referenced column.
user_visible_surface: JSON deparse format: "fmt" strings with %{...} placeholders plus named fields, editable before expansion.
C API: EventTriggerGetCollectedCommands() and EventTriggerCollectAlterColumnTypeUsing() in event_trigger.h; new ddl_deparse.h header.
Test module test_ddl_deparse with GUCs test_ddl_deparse.print_deparsed_ddl ('json|text|both') and test_ddl_deparse.execute_deparsed_ddl.
Planned, not in this series: a DDL WAL record and a logical replication protocol message carrying xid, flags, LSN, relid and versioned JSON with the executing role.
author_claims: Preserving user intent lets a replay use the defaults of the target, such as default TOAST compression across major versions.
Deparsing the parse tree recovers information that WAL or catalogs lack, such as the USING expression.
The v2 series fixes bugs in the earlier patch, including non-executable UNIQUE ... USING INDEX TABLESPACE output and a lost fillfactor.
001_deparse_regress.pl replays the core regression suite through the deparser and shows CREATE/ALTER TABLE commands deparse correctly.
DDL replication needs its own WAL record, because pg_logical_emit_message() is granted to PUBLIC and is unsafe for DDL apply.
brief.thread_state: Bharath Rupireddy, Vitaly Davydov and Nikhil Sontakke replied; Vitaly doubts parse-tree deparse and prefers decoding catalog changes from WAL, and Nikhil supports the intent-preserving design and sent fix patches. The author says an updated patch is coming, and the CommitFest entry needs a rebase.
unclear: The series adds no SQL-callable function, so it does not say how a user or extension other than the test module calls the deparser.
There is no documentation, and no stability promise for the JSON format or its version field.
Only CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE are covered, and there is no plan or estimate for other object types.
CTAS handling, with its two output modes and schema-only capture point, has no design beyond the thread.
The thread does not say how this relates to or overlaps the pg_get_table_ddl() proposal if both land.
Commit messages leave Author lines empty and note credit for the earlier deparse patch is still missing.

prior_attempts.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands
prior_attempts.quote: As presented, this stuff has an extremely high maintenance cost long-term because it requires anybody doing a change in the parsed tree structures of the DDLs replicated to also change the code paths introduced by this patch set.
prior_attempts.reason: Michael Paquier objected that the hand-written deparser, with its one-to-one mapping of node enums to hardcoded text, makes every change to the parse node structures of replicated DDL also require a change here. He asked for generated code instead, and the authors argued that much of the deparsing cannot be generated. Work stopped after July 2023, and in March 2024 Amit Kapila said the entry should be closed because it still needs a lot of work.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: This version keeps user intent, covers only CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE, and replays the core regression suite through the deparser. It moves the WAL record and the protocol message to a later series.

objections.title: Hand-written deparser keeps the maintenance cost that stopped the earlier patch
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a clause to CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE and does not touch ddl_deparse.c. If the change makes the deparser decline the command, 001_deparse_regress.pl only prints a count. If the deparser drops the clause and no later test output depends on it, the replay also passes, and DDL replication users find the missing clause only when the subscriber schema differs.
objections.argument: The earlier DDL replication patch [P1] ended over this cost: every change to the parse node structures of replicated DDL must also change the deparser. This series is still a hand-written mapping from parse nodes to text. The 0002 commit message says declined commands are reported, not asserted, and the 0004 message says the replay cannot check rules that leave the same catalogs. Message #10 calls the detection reliable, but no message answers the [P1] objection or discusses generated code.
objections.author_must_show: What makes a grammar or parse-node change fail a test when the patch forgets ddl_deparse.c, including clauses that leave the catalogs unchanged?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

critic.reasoning: [P1] concerns the same hand-written design, so the precedent applies. Message #10 calls detection reliable, but the 0002 message says declined commands are only counted and the 0004 message says replay cannot check rules that leave the catalogs the same.

objections.title: Implicit object names diverge between publisher and subscriber on replay
objections.failure_scenario: A subscriber already holds a relation named t_a_seq. `create table t (a serial)` replays as serial, so the subscriber names its sequence t_a_seq1. A later replicated `alter sequence public.t_a_seq ...` then changes the wrong sequence or fails, and apply stops or the schemas drift without notice.
objections.argument: The v2-0001 commit message says a serial column is kept as serial and a clause the user did not write is not emitted. The subscriber then picks the names of implicit objects, such as the sequence and possibly the constraints and indexes. Later deparsed ALTER and DROP commands use the names from the publisher's catalogs, as the identity fields in message #14 show. The proposal does not say how a replayed command and the commands after it agree on these names.
objections.author_must_show: How does the subscriber end up with the same names as the publisher for implicit sequences, constraints and indexes when its namespace already differs?

critic.reasoning: Keeping serial as serial and omitting unwritten names lets the subscriber choose implicit names, while later commands carry the publisher's names. No message says how the two agree when the subscriber's namespace already differs.

objections.title: Session settings that shape the table are lost on the subscriber
objections.failure_scenario: A session runs `set default_tablespace = 'fast'` or sets default_table_access_method, then `create table t (a int)`. The deparser omits the clause because the user did not write it. The apply worker runs with its own settings, so the subscriber puts t in another tablespace or access method, and nobody sees the difference until a failover.
objections.argument: In message #5 the author treats a default as replaceable by the target's default, using default_toast_compression as the example. A session SET of the same setting is also an explicit choice, but the rule in v2-0001 cannot tell it apart from no choice at all. The planned envelope in message #14 carries the role but no session settings. Vitaly's question in message #8 about which settings to replicate is still open.
objections.author_must_show: Which session settings does the deparser treat as user intent, and how does the planned envelope bring them to the apply worker?

critic.reasoning: Message #5 covers server-wide defaults only. A session `set` of default_tablespace or default_table_access_method is a user choice that the omit rule drops, and message #9 leaves open which settings count as intent.

objections.title: The JSON format becomes a cross-version contract with no stability rules
objections.failure_scenario: A newer publisher emits a fmt string with a field or clause the older subscriber's expander does not know, during a major-version upgrade, which is the main replication use case. The subscriber either fails apply or expands SQL it cannot run. Nobody has defined which side should handle that.
objections.argument: The format already changed between the patch in message #1 and v1 in message #10, with new placeholders and new fields. The "version" field shows up only in the planned envelope in message #14, and the series has no documentation for the format. Because fmt strings carry SQL syntax from the publisher, the expander alone cannot downgrade a command for an older target.
objections.author_must_show: What compatibility rule will the JSON format follow across major versions, and what does an older subscriber do with a field or clause it does not know?

critic.reasoning: Message #14 plans a version field but gives no rule for a field or clause the subscriber does not know. The scenario's direction is wrong for upgrades, where the publisher is older, but replication from a newer to an older server is still unanswered.

objections.title: Deparser lands in core with no in-core caller or SQL entry point
objections.failure_scenario: Core ships ddl_deparse.c and ddl_json.c, but only the test module calls them, and DDL replication arrives in a later series or not at all. Every later grammar change to CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE must also update the deparser. Users get no feature, and committers carry the upkeep from the first release.
objections.argument: The 0001 commit message says nothing in the tree calls the deparser, and the series adds no SQL function. In message #7 the author agrees that logging, auditing and WAL mining can be handled outside core, which leaves future DDL replication as the only core consumer. The small pieces an extension cannot add itself, EventTriggerGetCollectedCommands() and the USING capture in tablecmds.c, could go in alone so that the deparser can mature as an extension. The in-tree regression replay is a real benefit, but it guards code with no user yet.
objections.author_must_show: Why should the deparser enter core before the DDL replication series that consumes it, instead of only the collection hooks while the deparser lives in an extension?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

critic.reasoning: Infrastructure-first ordering is accepted practice, but message #12 defers the consumer until the deparser patches settle, and message #7 leaves replication as the only core use. [P1] must not be used as support here, because that patch set included its consumer.

other_surviving.title: Auditing and schema sync are named as users but conceded in thread
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An audit or schema-sync extension author reads the commit message and expects to use the deparser. They find no SQL-callable function and no stable, documented JSON format. They keep logging the query text from a utility hook, as message #6 suggests.
other_surviving.argument: The 0001 commit message lists auditing and schema synchronization as intended consumers. In message #7 the author agrees that logging, auditing and WAL mining can be handled outside core, which leaves DDL replication as the only use case. The series ships no callable interface for those other groups, so their demand does not support the core cost.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which non-replication users have asked for an in-core intent-preserving deparser, and what interface in this series would they call?

critic.reasoning: The 0001 commit message names auditing and schema synchronization as consumers, but message #7 says they can be handled outside core. The series offers them only a C accessor added for the test module.

refuted.title: Omitting unwritten clauses loses settings that came from session GUCs
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs `set default_table_access_method = 'columnar'` or `set default_tablespace = fast`, then `create table t (a int)`. The deparser emits no clause, so the subscriber creates a heap table in its own default tablespace. Nothing reports the difference, and the user finds it when performance or disk usage differs.
refuted.argument: The commit message for 0001 says a clause the user did not write is not emitted, so a replay adopts whatever default is in effect where it runs. The TOAST compression argument in message #5 covers server-wide defaults. It does not cover session or role GUCs, where the user did choose the value, just not in the statement text. Here the deparser treats an explicit choice as no choice.
refuted.author_must_show: How does the deparser treat values taken from session-level settings such as default_tablespace, default_table_access_method and default_toast_compression, and which of them does it emit?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2, which also ties the gap to the planned envelope and to the open question in message #8.

refuted.title: No user-callable interface, yet auditing and schema sync are named
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator writes an audit event trigger in PL/pgSQL, following the example in message #1, but ddl_deparse_to_json() no longer exists. Only C code using EventTriggerGetCollectedCommands() can reach the deparser. If a SQL function arrives later, its shape will be fixed by the replication message format and not by the use cases cited now.
refuted.argument: The 0001 commit message names auditing and schema synchronization as consumers, but it also says nothing in the tree calls the deparser. Its only accessor is a C function added for the test module. Message #7 states that auditing does not need an in-core deparser. That leaves the user-facing surface for those uses undefined, and the cited benefits beyond replication unsupported.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the series expose a SQL-callable deparse and expand function, and if not, how is an audit or schema-sync user expected to use the deparser?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-2. Both say the 0001 commit message names auditing and schema synchronization, while message #7 concedes those uses and the series has no SQL-callable function.

refuted.title: Hand-written deparser must track every future CREATE/ALTER TABLE change
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new CREATE TABLE option and touches only gram.y and tablecmds.c. The core regression output does not show the option's catalog effect, so the deparser drops it and 001_deparse_regress.pl stays green. A DDL replication subscriber then builds the table without the option, and a user finds out after the release ships.
refuted.argument: [P1] was withdrawn after an objection that a hand-written deparser forces every change to the replicated parse nodes to also change the deparser. This series keeps that design and covers about 170 KB of code for two commands only. The replay test catches only differences that show up in regression output. Patch 0004 states that intent rules such as omitting unwritten clauses cannot be checked by replay, and declined commands are counted, not asserted.
refuted.author_must_show: What makes a patch that adds a CREATE or ALTER TABLE clause fail loudly when it does not update ddl_deparse.c, including clauses whose effect is invisible in regression output?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which states the same maintenance concern with the same evidence from the 0002 and 0004 commit messages.

refuted.title: A second table-DDL renderer next to pg_get_table_ddl and pg_dump
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer adds a new table storage option and updates pg_dump and pg_get_table_ddl() but not the deparser, or the reverse. The three renderers then emit different SQL for the same table. Users of DDL replication and users of the SQL function see different results, and nobody notices until a replica diverges.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says the project should not maintain two features with similar function and asks whether pg_get_table_ddl() should be extended instead. Message #7 narrows the deparser's unique value to telling written clauses from defaults for replication. The series does not say how the deparser and pg_get_table_ddl() share code, or which one owns the rendering of a table option.
refuted.author_must_show: Which rendering code do the deparser, pg_get_table_ddl() and pg_dump share, so that adding a table option means updating one place rather than three?

critic.reasoning: Messages #3 and #7 explain that pg_get_table_ddl() cannot tell written clauses from defaults and does not cover ALTER TABLE, and the 0001 message says expressions and constraints come from ruleutils. The remaining risk of a forgotten deparser update is prior-attempts-1.

refuted.title: Deparser lands with no in-tree consumer and an unstated JSON contract
refuted.failure_scenario: The deparser is committed and extensions start to parse its JSON through EventTriggerGetCollectedCommands(). The later DDL replication design needs a different JSON shape or a CTAS capture point. Changing the format then breaks those extensions, and keeping it constrains replication.
refuted.argument: Patch 0001 states that nothing in the tree calls the deparser, and the only caller is a test module. The WAL record, the protocol message, CTAS capture and the version field appear only in messages #12 and #14 as future work. Message #7 states that replication is the single use case that justifies an intent-preserving deparser in core. Committing the deparser first means the project keeps the code and its format before the consumer that defines its requirements exists.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the deparser and the DDL replication consumer be reviewed and committed together, and what stability does the JSON format promise to extensions before then?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1 for the missing consumer and of standards-compat-2 for the format contract. The extension-breakage scenario is weak, because Postgres does not promise a stable C API across major versions.

refuted.title: Deparser lands with no consumer while its upkeep starts at once
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer adds a new CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE clause. They must also extend ddl_deparse.c, or 001_deparse_regress.pl flags the gap. No user gains anything from that work until a DDL replication series lands, and that series has not been posted.
refuted.argument: The 0001 commit message says nothing in the tree calls the deparser, and only the test module uses it. The WAL record, the protocol message and the capture infrastructure are planned follow-ups (messages #12, #14). Demand for DDL replication is long-standing. But this series makes every author of table DDL pay for the deparser now, and the benefit depends on later patches. [P1] was withdrawn over this same per-syntax maintenance cost, without a shipped consumer to justify it.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the deparser be committed together with a working DDL replication consumer, or which user benefits from it in the release where it lands alone?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1. Its use of [P1] also does not fit, because that patch set included WAL logging and apply and so had a consumer.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-2: Session settings that shape the table are lost on the subscriber

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: Logical replication of DDL is the motivating consumer, and a DDL WAL record is planned for a later series.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: A logical replication protocol message carrying versioned JSON is planned, so the JSON format becomes a cross-version contract.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-1: Implicit object names diverge between publisher and subscriber on replay

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The series adds EventTriggerGetCollectedCommands(), EventTriggerCollectAlterColumnTypeUsing() and the new ddl_deparse.h header.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-2: The JSON format becomes a cross-version contract with no stability rules

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The planned envelope carries the executing role, and a subscriber would run the expanded DDL.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-2: The JSON format becomes a cross-version contract with no stability rules

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: ddl_deparse.c is a hand-written mapping that every later CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE syntax change must update.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: Message #7 agrees auditing and logging can live outside core, and no in-tree code calls the deparser yet.

questions: What makes a patch that adds a CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE clause fail a test when it does not update ddl_deparse.c, including clauses that leave the catalogs unchanged?
How does the subscriber get the same names as the publisher for implicit sequences, constraints and indexes when its namespace already differs?
Which session settings, such as default_tablespace and default_table_access_method, does the deparser treat as user intent, and how do they reach the apply worker?
What compatibility rule does the JSON format follow across major versions, and what does a subscriber do with a field or clause it does not know?
Why should the deparser enter core before the DDL replication series that uses it, instead of only the collection hooks?

committability.owner_note: The visible thread and CommitFest entry do not identify any participant as a committer. The owner would need to know logical replication, event triggers and the utility command code in tablecmds.c.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a hand-written deparser that must follow every later change to table DDL syntax, and for a JSON format that becomes a cross-version replication contract once the consumer lands.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a v2 series, moved the CommitFest entry forward and says an updated patch is coming. Nikhil Sontakke also sent fix patches.

priority.reason: DDL replication has lasting demand among logical replication users, but the series is about 250 KiB for two commands and keeps the maintenance design that [P1] was withdrawn over. Code review is premature until the list agrees on the maintenance answer and on the replay semantics for implicit names and session settings.

provisional_note: Only 3 of 14 messages and no code were read. Not checked: whether expressions from ruleutils are schema-qualified independently of search_path, and how the deparser handles commands it declines.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands
precedents_retrieved.authors: Zheng Li (zhengli), Zhijie Hou (houzj), Ajin Cherian (ajinc), vigneshwaran C (vignesh.postgres), Runqi Tian (runqitian)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replicate DDL commands through logical replication so that schema changes reach subscribers, for example during major version upgrades. The later patch set deparses DDL commands in event triggers into a JSON format string, WAL-logs it, and the apply worker rebuilds and runs the command, starting with create, alter and drop table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the hand-written deparser, with its one-to-one mapping of node enums to hardcoded text, makes every change to the parse node structures of replicated DDL also require a change here. He asked for generated code instead, and the authors argued that much of the deparsing cannot be generated. Work stopped after July 2023, and in March 2024 Amit Kapila said the entry should be closed because it still needs a lot of work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As presented, this stuff has an extremely high maintenance cost long-term because it requires anybody doing a change in the parsed tree structures of the DDLs replicated to also change the code paths introduced by this patch set.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix NULL dereference in pg_get_database_ddl()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a NULL check in pg_get_database_ddl_internal() so that a dattablespace pointing to a missing tablespace no longer crashes the backend in pg_strcasecmp(). In that case the function omits the TABLESPACE clause, and a regression test covers it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The only reproducer was a manual update of pg_database with allow_system_table_mods, and David Rowley asked why this self-inflicted catalog corruption should matter more than other such cases. The author then found no supported path to the state, because the catalog snapshot keeps both lookups consistent and DROP TABLESPACE fails while the database directory exists, so he withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Can you explain why this method of self-inflicted catalogue corruption
is any more important than any of the just-about-infinite other ways
there are of causing issues by manually updating the catalogue tables?

precedents_retrieved.title: Make deparsing of column defaults faster
precedents_retrieved.summary: Jeff Janes proposed passing zero instead of the relation OID as the second argument to pg_get_expr when deparsing column defaults (in pg_dump, psql and other callers), on the grounds that defaults cannot contain Vars, which avoids building a deparse context and made pg_dump -s on a 1600-column table about 40 times faster. Peter Eisentraut offered an alternative patch that caches the deparse context in fn_extra of pg_get_expr across calls.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut noted that his in-progress generated columns patch would remove the assumption that defaults contain no Vars, and later that more work was needed to cover dumping and restoring tables with many columns, in particular the pg_restore slowness (deparse_context_for called from StoreAttrDefault) and check constraints. The author said he would pursue a different approach, a hash table for making column names unique, in a future commitfest, and asked for the entry to be closed. Peter Eisentraut marked it returned with feedback until a more complete solution exists.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm going to set this thread as returned with feedback until we have a
more complete solution.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert recent SQL/JSON related commits
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert recent SQL/JSON related commits
Reverted commit(s): SQL/JSON: Fix JSON_TABLE() column deparsing; SQL/JSON: Fix default ON ERROR behavior for JSON_TABLE; SQL/JSON: Avoid initializing unnecessary ON ERROR / ON EMPTY steps
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Reverts 68222851d5a8, 565caaa79af, and 3a97460970f, because a few
BF animals didn't like one or all of them.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Pavel Stehule, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to), and in v2 json_translate, which recursively replaces every value, including array elements, that exactly equals a given string with another string. The author meant it for mapping categorical or enum values deep inside a document, in the style of the Unix tr utility.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan judged blind replacement of every instance of a string, regardless of context, to be a niche use and asked why it could not be an extension. Pavel Stehule suggested using JsonPath to say what to replace, and Peter Eisentraut pointed to json_transform in Oracle and the SQL standard draft, noting that json_transform and json_translate together might confuse users. The thread ends there, and the author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Blindly replacing every
instance of a single string regardless of context seems at best a niche
use. Is there any reason not to make this an extension?

precedents_retrieved.title: Fixes a trivial bug in dumped parse/query/plan trees
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the leading space that the node output code writes after the opening parenthesis when it dumps an array field, so "( 1 4)" becomes "(1 4)". The author called the space a bug in the dumped parse, query and plan trees.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson and Tom Lane said the format is intentional and that changing it could break external parsers of the node format. Tom Lane said the space is a skipped minor optimization and that a small saving in isolation does not justify the risk to third-party code. He would accept such breakage only for a large cut in stored parse tree size, about 2X or better.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
While our existing nodeRead code wouldn't have a
problem with removing the extra whitespace, I share your fear that
we could introduce bugs into some third-party code somewhere.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical insert/update/delete WAL records for custom table AMs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add new WAL records representing a logical insert, update, delete (and later truncate) that do nothing at REDO time and are only processed during logical decoding, so that custom table AMs such as a columnar extension can support logical decoding/replication without extensible WAL. Later versions added SQL functions pg_logical_emit_insert/update/delete/truncate and tests using test_decoding.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch, saying that with custom WAL resource managers (his parallel extensible rmgr work) it had become less important to him. Earlier, Amit Kapila questioned whether a common heap-tuple-based format could work for all table AMs, and the patch had stopped applying, but the visible messages show no deciding objection from a reviewer.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Withdrawn for now. With custom WAL resource managers this is less
important to me.

precedents_retrieved.title: Xact event callback at command start
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a way for an extension to run code before each SQL statement in a transaction, so that it can implement server-side statement-level rollback. Early versions used hooks around start_xact_command(), later versions used a new XACT_EVENT_COMMAND_START event for xact callbacks, and v5 went back to a hook called after start_xact_command().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Tom Lane objected to exposing an API for statement-level rollback in an extension, because top-level transaction state is tied to backend internals and the hook placements would be fragile and add overhead to the exec_* functions in postgres.c. Andres Freund added that a real solution needs core work, such as making subtransactions cheap enough to avoid xid wraparound, and that these hooks do not move toward it. Tom Lane also said the new xact callback events were the wrong design, since they broke postgres_fdw. After this, the author said there was no chance of inclusion and offered to withdraw the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm *very* unconvinced it makes sense to implement a feature like this in an extension / that we should expose API for that purpose. To me the top-level transaction state is way too tied to our internals for it to be reasonably dealt with in an extension.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add OID descriptions to dumped parse/query/plan trees
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds comments to the text dumps of parse, query and plan trees that name the object behind each OID, such as the index, operator, function or type. It does this by catalog lookups inside the node output code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the lookups would make the dump code need a live, non-aborted transaction and could add catalog accesses that cause problems or deadlocks, so pprint could no longer be called from almost anywhere. He also said the change breaks re-reading of dumped trees, which rules, views and parallel query depend on. The author withdrew the patch after this reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It means that the dump code has to
execute in a live (not-aborted) transaction, which is not a
requirement it had before, and will complicate some debugging
scenarios.

precedents_retrieved.title: Time-delayed logical replication subscriber

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 24c35ec and 57169ad.  PreRestoreCommand() and
PostRestoreCommand() need to be put closer to the system() call calling
a restore_command, as they enable in_restore_command for the startup
process which would in turn trigger an immediate proc_exit() in the
SIGTERM handler.  Perhaps we could get rid of this behavior entirely,
but 24c35ec has made the window where the flag is enabled much larger
than it was, and any Postgres-like actions (palloc, etc.) taken by code
paths while the flag is enabled could lead to more severe issues in the
shutdown processing.

Note that curculio has showed that there are much more problems in this
area, unrelated to this change, actually, hence the issues related to
that had better be addressed first.  Keeping the code of HEAD in line
with the stable branches should make that a bit easier.

Per discussion with Andres Freund and Nathan Bossart.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use indexes on the subscriber when REPLICA IDENTITY is full on the publisher
precedents_retrieved.summary: Use indexes on the subscriber when REPLICA IDENTITY is full on the publisher

roaster_notes.note: One objection only. [P7] is about logical WAL records for table AMs and does not fit. Message #1 points to two earlier deparse threads, but the visible material does not report why they stopped.
Three objections raised. Overlap with pg_get_table_ddl() was discussed in messages #1 and #7 and is left to other angles.

The series adds no WAL record, catalog change, on-disk format or protocol message. Those are only planned, so these objections are about the replication semantics the intent-preserving design commits to, and the planned record cannot be checked yet.

The series adds no privilege surface. It has no SQL-callable function and no new catalog or GUC outside the test module, and it runs only inside event triggers, which need superuser. Its catalog reads stay within what the trigger owner can already see. Security concerns belong to the planned DDL WAL record and protocol message, which are not in this series. One open point there is how a subscriber maps the "role" field in the JSON, a role name taken from the publisher, to its own privileges. Message #14 already rejects pg_logical_emit_message() because it is granted to PUBLIC. One point needs the code: whether expressions taken from ruleutils are schema-qualified independently of the session search_path.
pg_get_table_ddl() is still a proposal, so it is not an existing alternative, and the author explains why catalog-state output cannot preserve user intent.

Demand for DDL replication itself is real and has lasted: several prior attempts, plus engaged reviewers from more than one company. The objections concern this series shipping the deparser ahead of that consumer.
